Formation_Explanation: Tamil/Malayalam high-i transitive stem supports high-i branch; exact mpp versus pp is comparative morphology.

Full_Derivation: K03: *aẓ-i-ntt > *aẓ-i-cc > inscriptional ẓaccu; *aẓ-i-mpp > *ẓapp- > Telugu ḍappi. Palatalization after i must precede deletion of its conditioning vowel under this account. Initial ẓ>ḍ follows displacement in the labial formation; the inscriptional palatal formation directly attests the otherwise hidden initial-ẓ stage. These are related tense/voice formations, not two independent sound-change events.
Exception_Notes: Sastri 1969 pp.310–311, inscription38 (dated there 890 CE), has displaced ḻassi line14 and retained aḻisina lines20–21, aḻiputa line35 in one text, but different grammatical formations: coexistence is not identical-context free variation. Earlier inscription16 (pp.291–292, dated 670–680) has ḻaccina; DHARMA00026 distinguishes this reading from older editorial ḍaccina. ṛ̆assi and ḍappi are displaced, but ḍakkā has a different extension and remains uncertain. Parji/Gadaba killing forms have an explicit alternative d309. Homophonous thirst ḍappi d109 must not be merged solely by spelling.
References: K03 pp.194–195; DEDR 277; Sastri 1969 pp.291–292 inscription16, pp.310–311 inscription38, p.350 index; https://dharmalekha.info/texts/INSTelugu00026

Formation_Explanation: Low-vowel iṭaṟ and eḍaŋk are independent, but exact kk stem is not. Shortening after contraction is a hypothesis.

Formation_Explanation: Independent Tamil iraṇṭu. Low-vowel prediction gives earlier rēṇḍ, with later shortening needed for modern reṇḍu; historical long rēṇḍ forms are checked separately.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: K03 pp.159–160: *ir-aṇṭ > *eraṇḍ > hypothetical *rēṇḍ > Telugu reṇḍu with shortening before a nasal-stop cluster; other SCDr *ir-i/u-ṇṭ > *rīṇḍ with variable shortening and Konda backing to runḍi. Human *iru-var remains vowel-first in Telugu iruvuru and Gondi irvur; r+v assimilation yields Kannada/Old Telugu ibbar forms. Tamil/Malayalam/Tulu aphaeresis produces reṇṭu/raṇṭu/raḍḍɯ in later language histories. Malto *irw > iwr (corpus ivr) is a separate medial consonant transposition.
Exception_Notes: Do not count human, nonhuman, twenty, two hundred and ordinal derivatives as independent roots. Telugu retained iru/īr is a bound root and cannot be treated as an identical free-word input to reṇḍu. The short Telugu output does not prove that a long intermediate existed; *rēṇḍ is K03’s conditional reconstruction. Kui rīnḍe shows that pre-cluster shortening was not universal across languages. Konda iddum retains an initial vowel in a measure compound and needs separate cluster-assimilation/contact analysis. Kodagu daṇḍɨ, Markodi dad and Badaga ratte require local phonological/contact histories; do not automatically equate them with the SCDr innovation. Kurux ēṇḍ has a vowel history K03 explicitly calls puzzling. Toda ačok/acok is a measure term within an example, not another reflex of two.
References: DEDR 474 p.46 directly checked; K03 pp.159–160 and p.116; Hockings–Pilot-Raichoor 1992 pp.54,86,507; Canvin 2025 lect data

Exception_Notes: The pancake head is not the only reconstructed input of this etymon. Counting all members as geminate-root exclusions would discard eligible singleton derivatives. Conversely the geminate pancake alone does not test movement of a singleton. Telugu aḍasāla contains a separate kitchen component and may be regionally transmitted. Badaga aṭra/attara hot variants require local cluster/epenthesis history, not the initial metathesis examined here; nāgaṭṭte plant name has uncertain linkage.
References: DEDR 76; K03 pancake reconstruction in CLDF

Formation_Explanation: Independent low-ay nominal form remains vowel-initial.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.

Formation_Explanation: Retained related measure formation beside lāvu; final i/u history is separate.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *aḷ-av > *ḷāv > lāvu in Telugu, with separate ḷ>l. Related palatal extensions give Kuvi/Pengo lāc and Kui ḍās/ḍāc, requiring local lateral-to-stop correspondence. Tulu aḷapuni > lappuni is compatible with aphaeresis and strengthening; K03 p.117 explicitly groups its short-vowel counterpart under aphaeresis.

Manda lēc has unexplained e, so quantity/quality tests exclude it pending a supported vowel history. Badaga ādu measured has an explicitly cited archaic aldu precursor, evidence for lateral loss plus contraction/lengthening, not promotion. Toda’s Q in the DEDR digital tense string is a transcription issue; retain raw data and use independent Toda citation for order.
References: DEDR 295; K03 p.117; Hockings & Pilot-Raichoor 1992 pp.4,38,43 (citing Emeneau 1939 p.46)

Formation_Explanation: Independent root low a, but matching labial suffix less secure than -ay.

Brahui ha in and hatining are associated morphological comparisons in the source; they are not independently counted as three reflexes of this root. Formation_Explanation: Human suffix is independently contrasted with nonhuman aṇṭ; one numeral family.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: K03 pp.159–160: *ir-aṇṭ > *eraṇḍ > hypothetical *rēṇḍ > Telugu reṇḍu with shortening before a nasal-stop cluster; other SCDr *ir-i/u-ṇṭ > *rīṇḍ with variable shortening and Konda backing to runḍi. Human *iru-var remains vowel-first in Telugu iruvuru and Gondi irvur; r+v assimilation yields Kannada/Old Telugu ibbar forms. Tamil/Malayalam/Tulu aphaeresis produces reṇṭu/raṇṭu/raḍḍɯ in later language histories. Malto *irw > iwr (corpus ivr) is a separate medial consonant transposition.
Exception_Notes: Do not count human, nonhuman, twenty, two hundred and ordinal derivatives as independent roots. Telugu retained iru/īr is a bound root and cannot be treated as an identical free-word input to reṇḍu. The short Telugu output does not prove that a long intermediate existed; *rēṇḍ is K03’s conditional reconstruction. Kui rīnḍe shows that pre-cluster shortening was not universal across languages. Konda iddum retains an initial vowel in a measure compound and needs separate cluster-assimilation/contact analysis. Kodagu daṇḍɨ, Markodi dad and Badaga ratte require local phonological/contact histories; do not automatically equate them with the SCDr innovation. Kurux ēṇḍ has a vowel history K03 explicitly calls puzzling. Toda ačok/acok is a measure term within an example, not another reflex of two.
References: DEDR 474 p.46 directly checked; K03 pp.159–160 and p.116; Hockings–Pilot-Raichoor 1992 pp.54,86,507; Canvin 2025 lect data

Formation_Explanation: Independent matching-u clothing formation is a retained eligible control.

Indo-Aryan *ōḍḍh clothing words are linked contact comparisons and do not determine the Dravidian reconstruction. Toda non-Toda dress noun may reflect cultural diffusion and does not add a separate root.
References: DEDR 587; DEN1 p.401 additions; linked CDIAL 2547 kept separate

Formation_Explanation: Medial syncope and assimilation explain absent r; O rather than secure retained-apical evidence.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.

Exception_Notes: Kui is genuinely mixed within one source, so its retained forms cannot be coded missing or assigned to a separate outcome-defined root. Kuvi uku/ukku steel may be a regional technical loan or parallel medial assimilation; either way it is not the same displaced melt formation as rūy. d656 burn is a plausible parent-root relation, to be collapsed in sensitivity counts.

Formation_Explanation: Tamil/Malayalam independently support geminate; morphology genuinely distinguishes this from singleton locative.

Full_Derivation: *uḷ-a-n > *oḷan > *ḷōn > lōn gives Telugu lōna/lōnu and comparable Gondi lōn/rōn, with final suffix history differing by language. *uḷḷ-am > ullamu retains order. Konda olbi and Kuvi oṛp/onp thought verbs preserve initial V with internal consonant development.
Exception_Notes: DEDR dates oḷana to the seventh century and ḷōna to the ninth–tenth; a corpus lōna record incorrectly inherits the seventh-century date. These are source dating claims. The candidate seventh-century witness at Inpuḻōli has oḷana only in an older edition: Sastri1969 p.285 n.1 and DHARMA00099 read ēḷan ruling. Unless another inscription is identified, do not use oḷana to establish retention in seventh-century Telugu. Kui lai cannot be explained by the same o outcome without another vowel/formation history. Telugu submit loŋgu/loggu series is queried; Central Dravidian lopal may be Telugu loans. Brahui house urā and heart ust have explicit alternative etymologies; exclude them from secure core counts. An existence/inside common ancestor is plausible but not settled.
References: DEDR 698 p.68 directly checked; K03 *uḷḷ-am and *oḷ-an records

Formation_Explanation: Full bean formation; medial apical assimilation yields uddulu, an O outcome rather than secure apical retention.

Full_Derivation: *uẓ-unt > *ur-nd > *ur-d > udd, with nasal/stop simplification and assimilation, is a schematic route to Telugu uddulu. Exact sequencing of nasal loss and r assimilation may differ; Kannada urdu : uddu directly supports the latter step.
Exception_Notes: This same-u comparison retains the initial vowel despite the shared approximant found in displaced comb/tiger. Crop-name borrowing can spread either full or reduced forms, so branch distribution cannot by itself date each sound change. Marathi/Prakrit urad names are contact comparisons, not independent evidence for Dravidian metathesis.
References: DEDR 690 p.67 directly checked; K03 *uẓ-untu reconstruction

Formation_Explanation: Independent high-u thunder formation retains order.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *uṟ-um > Telugu uṟumu retains order, while conditional *oṟ-al > *ṟōl > ṟōlu/rōlu gives a displaced lament derivative. Kui *uṟ-um > *ṟūm > rūma/rūmba combines initial displacement/contraction with labial formation. Telugu roppu/rollu requires consonantal-suffix reconstruction or later shortening, not simply one uniform vowel input.
Exception_Notes: Expressive sound words can converge independently; do not use their semantic resemblance as decisive cognacy. Kui ṛunja is explicitly queried and has an unexplained nasal-palatal formation. Kannada ṟoppu could be an independent development or a regional loan; Brahui hūrra has an explicit Balochi comparison. Keep these separate from secure retained thunder forms and probable displaced lament forms.

Formation_Explanation: Long numeral contrasts with independently short tens compound.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *eẓ-(u)-pat > *ẓe-ppat > ḍebbadi is schematic: vowel loss, displacement, labial strengthening/voicing and the Telugu tens suffix require separate chronology. Later ḍebbʰai/ḍabbʰai adds suffix contraction, aspiration and e/a variation. Long *ēẓ-u > ēḍu retains order; no ad hoc shortening of modern ēḍu is required to feed seventy.
Exception_Notes: The compound boundary supplies independent conditioning information, but exact prehistoric weakening of u and voicing of p cannot be inferred merely from a compound label. The original ḍ in seventy remains distinct from later d elsewhere; orthography/source traditions need checking before claiming one universal merger date. K03 p.264 diagnoses Kolami seven forms as Telugu loans. Kui oḍgi is itself queried and has separate vowel/suffix history, not initial metathesis.

Formation_Explanation: Independent long southern grade; not a hidden reconstruction from retention.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *kiẓ-nd > *kẓind > krind > kind gives krinda/kinda. Displacement removes the front vowel from immediately after k, blocking Telugu k>c palatalization; later r-loss restores ki after that palatalization has ceased to act on this item. Long kīḍupaḍu retains the apical medially; krī may be a separate contraction or abbreviated derivative.
Exception_Notes: This is a relative chronology argument conditional on inheritance and the independently established palatalization environment, not proof from an isolated unpalatalized k. Do not shorten the citation root kīẓ ad hoc: a short allomorph is independently attested. Exact -nd and -nc history is less secure than initial order. Nilgiri/Brahui kī types admit medial-apical loss without displacement; they do not independently prove the Telugu route.
References: K03 p.128 Rule 14, p.158 Rule 21; DEDR 1619

Formation_Explanation: Tamil tiruku/Kannada tirugu match weak velar; contrast with trikku is independently morphological.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *tir-upp > *tir-pp > *tri-pp > trippu; *tir-ukk > *tir-kk > *tri-kk > trikku, with equal-vowel syncope/reassociation not requiring a literal audible vowel swap. *tir-uk > tirugu retains order. Kui trēba and Kuvi rēnai involve a different formative and initial t loss in the latter; its exact low-a/ high-i input must not be inferred solely from ē. Manda trīmba matches a nasal formation with long quantity.
Exception_Notes: A strong independently formed Telugu contrast: singleton-velar turn is retained while geminate causative/twist forms displace. This is evidence for morphological/cluster conditioning within a family, not a universal rule until other geminate and singleton inputs are tested. Trimmaṭa/trimmaru wandering need exact derivational reconstruction and are flagged less certain than trippu. Central tipp may result directly from medial r-p assimilation; Telugu tipiri may be analogical or metathetically restructured but does not prove initial tr loss. Badaga Tirikōṇa is a proper name and should not be an extra inherited turn witness.
References: DEDR 3246; K03 Rule 21; PSS83 p.229 nonautomatic application

Formation_Explanation: Independent low-a labial derivative remains full while velar crawl prāku changes.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *par-a-k > *prā-k > prāku, then r loss in pākul-āḍu, is the displaced crawl pathway; Tamil parakku supplies a matched velar formation but original gemination versus later simplification needs separate assessment. Telugu paracu/parapu/paragu retains order in other low-a formations. Kui prahpa/brāḍa and Kuvi pressali have distinct causative/voice extensions and vowel histories.
Exception_Notes: This is a genuine within-family lexical/morphological residual: low-a alone does not determine Telugu application, and the exact velar contrast cannot be repaired simply by assigning all crawl meanings to an invented class. Konda rēs metal plating may involve displaced *prēs with first-member loss, but e versus independently a requires another grade or contact and remains uncertain. Southern pammu/habbu/pabb and Gadaba pamp permit medial assimilation; do not invent hidden pr. Badaga initial p/h loss leaves r after a and is not metathesis.
References: DEDR 3949; K03 *par-a reconstruction; K61 immediate-antecedent principle

Formation_Explanation: Tamil vari supplies high-i formation, distinct from low-ay writing.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *war-ay > *wrāy > vrāyu > rāyu. Writing nouns vrā̃ta/vrālu and causative vrāyincu have distinct suffix histories. Telugu variyu metal-testing preserves the high-i formation. Kui vrīsa/Kuvi brīnai has high ī and different suffix history, potentially *war-i versus a different earlier vowel grade.
Exception_Notes: One first-member-loss word does not establish a universal low-vowel rule for wr clusters. Literacy vocabulary readily diffuses: Gondi/Konda/Kuvi rās/rāc and Gadaba rāyap may be Telugu exports or reflect local developments. Gondi varasānā retains full order, but its relation to a possible borrowed rās is uncertain. Telugu baruku and Parji varc have explicit alternative d5322 etymologies. Badaga finger/place-name homonyms attached to this group are not writing reflexes.

Formation_Explanation: Independent same-i stem retains order; vrīlu has another uncertain suffix.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: Conditional *wir-il > *wrīl > vrīlu gives the long displaced Telugu form if the suffix is established. *wir-i-nk > *wriŋk gives Kui vringa, while labial vrīva has its own quantity/formative history. Gondi rīk can follow *wrīk with w loss; source suffix comparison remains needed. Telugu viccu/vippu/vikku permits direct medial assimilation, independently paralleled by Kannada biccu and Tulu biccuni.

The broader displacement interpretation is stronger than the exact vowel/derivative chronology. Gondi rīk could involve regional borrowing or a distinct velar derivative; retain medium confidence. Kui birasakali is unshifted-looking but expressive/deverbal formation may differ. Sanskrit aravinda comparison concerns a compound and adds no independent root vote.
References: DEDR 5411; K61 p.67 §1.156 explicitly unattested derivative (prior verified reading); DEN1 1972 p.415 entry4438

Formation_Explanation: Independent comitative compound; Tulu aphaeresis has a separate history.
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: *oḍam#baḍ- > Tulu oḍam-baḍipuni beside dambaḍipuni by aphaeresis plus retroflex simplification; medial a remains and no output long vowel is required. Telugu oḍam/oḍã-baḍu has nasalization/loss at the boundary without initial apical movement. Grammatical -oṭu/-ōṭu and Toda -vɨṛ require their own clitic/prosodic history.
Exception_Notes: Tulu initial d is therefore not automatic evidence for the Telugu contraction process. Loss of initial o alone plus ḍ>d accounts for the observed segment sequence; a literal exchange would additionally need vowel fusion/loss and offers no independent advantage here. Badaga ōṭalu hotel with a following postposition gloss is a parser conflation, not a cognate comitative word. Morphological compounds and suffix allomorphs are not independent roots.

Gondi lum/lumm root/gore may be displaced but requires approximant-to-l and suffix history, and the gore comparison is explicitly queried. Tulu dappuni/aḍapuni has dialectal initial-vowel loss and a different vowel/root history; source corrections restore those forms from mistaken Kodagu labels. Tamil tunnu and Parji ḍukki are explicit Telugu loans. Agriculture-contact possibilities do not by themselves negate the deep comparative root.
References: K03 pp.152–153 example 86; PSS83 p.235 example 781; DEDR 688 p.67 directly checked

Formation_Explanation: Literary infinitive alternation is independently paired; grammatical nasal domain is not the classical apical rule.

Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.

Analogical stem extension and phonological reduction compete; passage-by-passage morphology is needed.
Exception_Notes: These are literary grammatical formations, not evidence that ordinary nasal roots joined the classical nonnasal apical rule. Formation_Explanation: Comparative oblique augment; mixed direct/oblique paradigm, not a lexical quantity test.
Outcome_Sources: DEDR1; source paradigm already preserved in linked database record; compare Krishnamurti2003 pp.222–223
Comparative_Panel_Scope: Cited retained-order comparanda; exact formation match is assessed in Input_Tier and explanation, not asserted for every panel form.
Full_Derivation: Proposed *ad-an-i > *daan-i > dāni; *aw-an-i > *waan-i > vāni, with modern plural vāṭi from a distinct *aw-att-i augment. Konda dani/vani can reflect subsequent shortening in obliques, but a directly contracted short outcome is not excluded. Telugu vā̃ḍu and Konda vānṟu require gender-formative history in addition to labial displacement. Konda abe/abeṇi : bān/bāṇi establishes a local labial-initial locative variant, with contraction and reformation not uniquely sequenced.
Exception_Notes: Count the distal and proximal entries as one deictic process family in the primary partition, not every inflected form as an independent root. Nominative adi and oblique dāni coexist by grammatical conditioning; simple claim all short V-apical words change is false. Labial participation is outside a narrowly apical lexical rule. K03 p.223 n.14 explicitly leaves shared Telugu–Konda innovation versus early Telugu borrowing unresolved. K03 p.222 n.13 proposes Old Telugu generalized the singular augment whereas spoken Telugu preserves *-att in the plural; this is a historical morphological hypothesis, not an independently dated sound change here. DEDR parser assigns obl broadly to whole paradigms and fragments Tamil forms/glosses; those tags are not all accurate POS analyses. Unrelated deictic compounds are preserved in full appendix but not counted as separate metatheses.

Formation_Explanation: Exact proximal prehistory depends on comparison with distal augment; high output may be analogical.

Full_Derivation: K03 proposes lowering in *id-an-i > *ed-an-i before displacement/contraction, followed by Konda deni, while Telugu dīni is remodeled to preserve the opposition to interrogative dēni; this is analogy, not a phonetic i+a>ī rule. Compare *iw-an-i > Konda veni versus Telugu vīni, modern plural vīṭi from *iw-att-i with corresponding analogical possibilities. Konda ibe/ibeṇi : bēn/bēṇi supplies labial locative restructuring; Pengo ibe/ibṇi retains initial i even with syncope.
Exception_Notes: The anti-homophony account for Telugu dīni is a plausible hypothesis (K03 p.223 n.14), not demonstrated by a directly attested earlier *deni stage. Sastri1969 pp.178,184 explicitly treats historical dēni as interrogative; an inscriptional English translation this grant is not sufficient to identify a proximal ancestral stage. Konda current DB plural oblique venka differs from K03 veni: preserve both source claims and do not silently replace morphology. Konda short deni versus long bēn shows formation-specific quantity. This cannot be used to validate a single phonetic outcome rule for all pronouns. Te nisuvu/nisũgu child is a separate semantic/cognacy issue within the giant deictic entry and is not evidence for nasal metathesis of the deictic base. Direct and oblique forms are research-split with links to their original unsplit database records.
